title: My morning
summary: Describe your morning routine with present-tense verbs: I wake up, I drink, I go.
intro: Arabic verbs show the person with a prefix: أَ for 'I' (أَذْهَبُ, I go), تَ for 'you' (تَذْهَبُ) and يَ for 'he' (يَذْهَبُ). Speaking to a woman, the verb also ends in ـِينَ: تَذْهَبِينَ. Join one action to the next with ثُمَّ (then).
objectives: Say five things you do every morning
Use present-tense verbs with I, you, he and she
Say when you do something: أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة

realLife.title: An early start
realLife.story: After being late yesterday, Daniel tells Layla about his new morning plan. Layla gets up even earlier than he does, and Sami admits that he often rushes out of the house without breakfast.

sentences.en: I wake up at seven o'clock.
sentences.literal: I wake up at the hour the seventh

sentences.en: I wash my face, then I drink tea.
sentences.literal: I wash my face, then I drink the tea

sentences.ar: هَلْ تَشْرَبِينَ الْقَهْوَة صَبَاحًا يَا لَيْلَى؟
sentences.en: Do you drink coffee in the morning, Layla?
sentences.literal: (question) you drink the coffee in the morning, O Layla

mistakes.why: Speaking to a woman, 'you drink' is tashrabīna, with the ending -īna.

sentences.ar: سَامِي يَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَة كُلَّ يَوْم.
sentences.en: Sami goes to school every day.
sentences.literal: Sami goes to the school every day
she goes out from the house early

mistakes.why: For 'she' the prefix is ta-, the same as for 'you' (to a man): takhruju.

sentences.en: You go to school by bus. (to a man)
sentences.literal: you go to the school by the bus

dialogue.title: A better morning
dialogue.culture: Many Egyptians start the day with strong, sweet tea or a small cup of coffee. A favourite breakfast is فُول (stewed fava beans) with warm flat bread, often bought from a street cart on the way to work.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا دَانْيَال! الْيَوْم أَنْتَ هُنَا مُبَكِّرًا. مَا السِّرّ؟
lines.en: Good morning, Daniel! Today you are here early. What's the secret?

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور! عِنْدِي سَاعَة جَدِيدَة، وَالْآن أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف.
lines.en: Good morning! I have a new watch, and now I wake up at half past six.
Excellent! And what do you do after that?

lines.ar: أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي، ثُمَّ أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَة وَآكُلُ خُبْزًا مَعَ جُبْن.
lines.en: I wash my face, then I drink coffee and eat bread with cheese.

lines.ar: أَنَا أَشْرَبُ الشَّاي بِالنَّعْنَاع صَبَاحًا. الْقَهْوَة قَوِيَّة جِدًّا لِي!
lines.en: I drink tea with mint in the morning. Coffee is too strong for me!
And you, Layla, when do you wake up?

lines.ar: أَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا جِدًّا، فِي السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة وَالنِّصْف، كُلَّ يَوْم.
lines.en: I wake up very early, at half past five, every day.

lines.ar: الْخَامِسَة وَالنِّصْف؟ لِمَاذَا؟ الدَّرْس فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة!
lines.en: Half past five? Why? The lesson is at nine o'clock!

lines.ar: أُكَلِّمُ أُمِّي فِي بَيْرُوت، ثُمَّ أَدْرُسُ الْكَلِمَات الْجَدِيدَة سَاعَةً.
lines.en: I call my mother in Beirut, then I study the new words for an hour.

lines.ar: وَمَتَى تَخْرُجِينَ مِنَ الْبَيْت؟ وَكَيْفَ تَذْهَبِينَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَة؟
lines.en: And when do you leave the house? And how do you get to school?
segs: you go out, you leave (to a woman)

lines.ar: أَخْرُجُ فِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة، وَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَة مَشْيًا. الْمَدْرَسَة قَرِيبَة.
lines.en: I leave at eight o'clock and walk to school. The school is close.

lines.ar: أَنَا أَذْهَبُ بِالْحَافِلَة، وَهِيَ بَطِيئَة جِدًّا فِي الصَّبَاح!
lines.en: I go by bus, and it is very slow in the morning!

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا أَصْدِقَاء! مَاذَا تَشْرَبُ يَا دَانْيَال؟ قَهْوَة؟
lines.en: Good morning, friends! What are you drinking, Daniel? Coffee?

lines.ar: نَعَم، قَهْوَة! أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَة كُلَّ صَبَاح، ثُمَّ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الصَّفّ.
lines.en: Yes, coffee! I drink coffee every morning, then I go to class.

lines.ar: وَأَنَا أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة، وَأَخْرُجُ مُسْرِعًا بِدُونِ فُطُور!
lines.en: And I wake up at eight o'clock and rush out without breakfast!

lines.ar: يَا سَامِي! الْفُطُور مُهِمّ جِدًّا فِي الصَّبَاح.
lines.en: Oh, Sami! Breakfast is very important in the morning.

reading.title: Daniel's morning
reading.ar: أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف. أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي، ثُمَّ أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَة. أَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْبَيْت فِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة، وَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَة بِالْحَافِلَة. الْآن أَنَا فِي الصَّفّ مُبَكِّرًا كُلَّ يَوْم.
reading.en: I wake up at half past six. I wash my face, then I drink coffee. I leave the house at eight o'clock and go to school by bus. Now I am in class early every day.

quiz.prompt: Fill the gap: 'Layla, do you drink tea?'
Which prefix shows 'I' in a present-tense verb?
In the dialogue, what time does Layla wake up?
Which verb has the rough kh sound of خ?

completion: Brilliant! You can describe your morning and use present-tense verbs with I, you, he and she.
